name: DECISION_V3_A_ADMISSION_MECHANISM_DIAGNOSIS_V1
purpose: Final outcome-blind descriptive diagnosis before Decision V4 design: test whether the observed A_SOFT durability advantage is associated with the magnitude of its preregistered relative rank-gap admission evidence, versus other candidate-history evidence, using only the already-consumed same-session diagnosis artifacts.

population.primary: A_SOFT entries inside the frozen paired-session population
population.reference: A_VACANCY rows may be counted only to verify the parent paired population; no new A_VACANCY policy construct is derived

frozen_questions: Within A_SOFT, is larger soft_rank_gap associated directionally with lower next-session severe-exit incidence?
Within completed A_SOFT spells, is larger soft_rank_gap associated directionally with lower eventual severe-exit incidence and longer holding duration?
Within the pre-existing candidate-evidence reporting strata, does the direction of the soft_rank_gap versus severe-incidence relationship persist?
Within paired sessions containing at least two A_SOFT entries with discordant next-session severe outcomes, does the larger-gap entry more often belong to the non-severe outcome?
Do candidate-history variables differ between A_SOFT entries that become severe next session and those that do not, indicating evidence beyond soft_rank_gap magnitude?
threshold_free_primary_statistics: Spearman correlation of soft_rank_gap with next_session_severe_exit
Spearman correlation of soft_rank_gap with eventual_severe_exit among completed entries
Spearman correlation of soft_rank_gap with duration_sessions
mean and median soft_rank_gap conditional on observed severe versus non-severe structural state
stop_rule: After this diagnosis is consumed, stop mechanism diagnosis and return to Decision V4 design/brainstorming; no additional descriptive rescue analysis without a separately justified new question.
interpretation_guard: This diagnosis can assess whether gap magnitude is associated with durability within the already-selected A_SOFT population. It cannot identify a causal effect of the >=5 hurdle itself because all A_SOFT entries already passed that hurdle, and it cannot authorize a numeric successor threshold.
